business_model.claim: Guardian sells pharmacy services: dispensing plus technology-enabled support that helps residents of long-term care facilities (LTCFs) stay on their drug regimens.
quotes: We are a leading, highly differentiated pharmacy services company that provides an extensive suite of technology-enabled services designed to help residents of LTCFs adhere to their appropriate drug regimen, which in turn helps reduce the cost of care and improve clinical outcomes.

business_model.claim: The company contracts directly with LTCFs to act as the principal pharmacy provider for their residents.
quotes: We enter into contracts directly with LTCFs to serve as the principal pharmacy provider for their residents.

business_model.basis: stated in P1; repeated in P4
business_model.claim: More than two-thirds of annual revenue comes from residents of assisted living facilities (ALFs) and behavioral health facilities (BHFs). Most of the rest comes from residents of skilled nursing facilities (SNFs).
quotes: More than two-thirds of our annual revenue for each of the past three years has been generated from residents of ALFs and BHFs, which are our target markets, while the remainder has been generated primarily from residents of skilled nursing facilities (“SNFs”).

business_model.claim: Revenue is recognized when prescriptions and other pharmacy services are delivered to the LTCF.
quotes: We recognize revenue at the time of delivery of prescriptions and other pharmacy services to the LTCF, at which time control has been transferred.

business_model.claim: A secondary revenue source is fee-based training and continuing education for LTCF staff.
quotes: We also offer training and continuing education programs to LTCF staff for a fee to educate caregivers on the proper administration of drugs to residents in accordance with the resident’s drug regimen.

business_model.claim: The network had 63 pharmacies, 57 of them full-service, serving approximately 218,000 residents in approximately 8,600 LTCFs across 39 states.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, our 63 pharmacies, 57 of which are full-service, served approximately 218,000 residents in approximately 8,600 LTCFs across 39 states.

business_model.claim: In ALFs and BHFs, a preferred-provider agreement does not deliver residents automatically. The sales team must win each resident, and these contracts can be ended on 30 days’ notice.
quotes: Instead, our sales team must market our pharmacy services to the individual residents in that community, each of whom has the right to choose their pharmacy provider.
These contracts can be terminated by either party generally upon 30 days’ notice.

business_model.claim: The stated growth strategy is to increase the number of residents served, both organically and through acquisitions.
quotes: Our core growth strategy focuses on increasing the number of residents we serve through a combination of organic and acquired growth.

business_model.claim: Full-year revenue rose from 1,228,409 to 1,448,685 (table in thousands), an increase of $220.3 million or 17.9%.
quotes: Revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $220.3 million or 17.9% compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

business_model.claim: Of that full-year increase, $68.4 million came from acquisitions and $151.9 million from organic growth.
quotes: $68.4 million of the increase was attributable to revenue from the Acquisitions, with the remaining $151.9 million of the increase attributable to the organic growth of our business.

business_model.claim: The full-year increase was driven by residents served rising from 186,000 to 205,000, prescriptions dispensed rising from 25.1 million to 28.6 million, and annual drug price inflation.
quotes: Further, the increase was attributable to increases in the number of residents served from 186,000 residents during December 2024 to 205,000 residents during December 2025 and prescriptions dispensed from 25.1 million during the year ended December 31, 2024 to 28.6 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, as well as annual drug price inflation.

business_model.claim: Negotiated prices under the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) on the first group of Part D drugs took effect, which reduces the per-prescription price on those drugs.
quotes: In January 2026, the initial ten Part D drugs that were part of IRA negotiations had their negotiated prices go into effect.

business_model.claim: Quarterly revenue fell from 377,427 to 371,070 (table in thousands). Acquisitions added $7.3 million, but organic revenue fell by $13.7 million, mainly because of IRA price cuts.
quotes: Excluding the $7.3 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.

business_model.claim: Over nine months, acquisitions added $38.4 million of revenue while organic revenue fell by $30.0 million.
quotes: Excluding the $38.4 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $30.0 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.

business_model.claim: Volumes kept growing despite the IRA price cuts: residents served rose from 204,000 to 218,000, and nine-month prescriptions dispensed rose from 21.0 million to 23.1 million.
quotes: Although organic revenue decreased due to IRA price reductions, the number of residents served increased from 204,000 residents during September 2025 to 218,000 residents during September 2026 and prescriptions dispensed increased from 21.0 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to 23.1 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold is mainly the cost of filling and delivering prescriptions, including the cost of buying the drugs. It also includes pharmacy personnel, delivery and supporting overhead.
quotes: Cost of goods sold consists primarily of expenses associated with the fulfillment and delivery of the prescription, including prescription drug acquisition costs.

business_model.basis: figures stated in P4 and F2; the cause is not shown in the evidence
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold as a share of revenue fell from 80.2% to 77.0% in the quarter and from 80.3% to 77.2% over nine months. Quarterly gross profit rose from 74,721 to 85,223 (table in thousands) even though revenue was lower.
Drug purchasing relies on wholesaler and manufacturer contracts that provide discounts, rebates and service fees, and on membership in the MHA group purchasing organization.
quotes: Our contracts with pharmaceutical wholesalers and manufacturers often provide us with, among other things, discounts on drugs we purchase, rebates and service fees.
We participate in the MHA group purchasing organization (“GPO”), for purposes of drug purchasing.

business_model.claim: Revenue depends on reimbursement from Medicare, Medicaid and private payors, and the company says it has limited bargaining power against payor demands for lower rates.
quotes: Given the significant competition in the industry, we have limited bargaining power to counter health plan payor demands for reduced reimbursement rates.
Any changes that lower reimbursement rates under Medicare, Medicaid or private payor programs could result in a substantial reduction in our revenues.

business_model.claim: Selling, general and administrative expenses are mainly personnel costs. They rose from 165,277 to 178,194 (table in thousands) over nine months.
quotes: Selling, general, and administrative expenses consist primarily of personnel-related expenses, including share-based compensation, salaries and benefits, for our employees at the pharmacies and support services engaged in other pharmacy related activities including sales and marketing, finance, legal, human resources, purchasing and other administrative functions.

business_model.claim: Labor is a major operating cost, so wage or staffing increases can reduce margins.
quotes: Because labor costs are and will continue to be a major component of our operating expenses, higher labor costs, whether as a result of increased wages or increased staffing levels, could reduce our profitability and gross margins.

business_model.claim: Nine-month share-based compensation expense fell from 12,770 to 7,528 (table in thousands), a decline within the personnel cost line.
The company uses automation (over 100 automated dispensing machines) and local delivery within about 200 miles of its pharmacies to support dispensing efficiency.
quotes: Specifically, we currently have over 100 automated dispensing machines deployed across our network.
We service LTCFs typically within a radius of 200 miles or less of our pharmacy locations, depending on the metropolitan area.

business_model.claim: Acquisitions add residents to the network. In the quarter the company bought Nautilus assets and moved that resident base into 18 existing pharmacies.
quotes: Guardian successfully transitioned the acquired resident base to 18 existing pharmacies within Guardian’s network, providing these communities access to Guardian's locally managed, high-touch pharmacy services.

material_events.claim: Negotiated prices for the first ten IRA Part D drugs took effect. Organic revenue in the third quarter fell by $13.7 million, which the filing attributes mainly to IRA pricing decreases.
quotes: In January 2026, the initial ten Part D drugs that were part of IRA negotiations had their negotiated prices go into effect.
Excluding the $7.3 million increase in revenue attributable to the Acquisitions, organic revenue decreased by $13.7 million, primarily attributable to pricing decreases as a result of the IRA.
